legislation.rule_description: s16(1): a person required to pay tax may deduct tax paid/payable by him on receipt of taxable services exclusively used in connection with the taxable services he provides, subject to holding a true and valid tax invoice not older than six tax periods; Authority may disallow/restrict per ss16A/16B/rules. s16(5): deduction excludes additional/further/extra tax, default surcharge, fine, penalty, fee. s16A: for transactions exceeding Rs 50,000, payment must be by crossed banking instrument from the business bank account of the service recipient, otherwise no input credit/adjustment/deduction/refund. s16B: long list of inadmissible input tax — includes (g)/(h) goods/services used in or for services taxed below 15% or at a specific non-value rate; (r) further/extra/value-addition tax under the Sales Tax Act 1990; (s) immovable-property/construction items except where directly used in the economic activity of persons paying tax at not less than 16%. s16C: input tax adjustment in a tax period capped at 80% of the output tax for that period.

legislation.name: The Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act, 2012

legislation.rule_description: s4(1): where a person provides taxable services in a Province other than Punjab but the recipient is resident in Punjab (or avails the services in Punjab) and tax is charged accordingly, the provider pays that tax to the Punjab Government. s4(2): a registered recipient of a taxable service deducts the whole tax and pays it to the Government. s4(3): a person providing taxable services in more than one Province including Punjab pays tax to Punjab to the extent charged from Punjab residents/persons availing services in Punjab. s4(4): service originating in Punjab but terminating outside Pakistan — tax payable to Punjab. s4(5): service originating outside Pakistan but received/terminating in Punjab — recipient liable. s3(3): a person's Punjab office/place of business and its non-Punjab office are treated as separate legal persons. s4(7): origin-principle disputes resolved under the Federal-Provincial understanding on reformed GST.

The original Schedule categories are: (1) hotels, marriage halls, lawns, clubs and caterers; (2) advertisement on TV and radio (with stated exclusions); (3) persons authorised to transact business on behalf of others — customs agents, ship chandlers, stevedores; (4) courier services; (5) beauty parlors, beauty clinics and slimming clinics; (6) laundries and dry cleaners.

risks.description: A service is mapped to the wrong schedule entry, tariff classification or exemption, so the wrong rate is charged or an exemption is wrongly claimed/denied. Each province has its own schedules and rates — a classification valid in one province does not transfer to another. Do not label a misclassification as evasion or fraud; it is a potential_error until investigated.
risks.exposure_note: Under-charged output tax (short payment) or over-charged tax passed to the customer.
risks.followup_action: Re-verify the classification against the transaction-date Schedule of the correct province; correct the invoice/return treatment; check whether the 2025 Sindh/Punjab schedule changes affect the entry.
risks.potential_financial_effect: Output tax difference between the applied rate and the correct rate, plus potential interest-like charges only where legally verified.
required_information: Service description and contract terms
Transaction-date Schedule entry and rate
Exemption conditions where claimed
risk_indicators: Rate applied differs from the Schedule entry for the service
Exemption claimed without a cited schedule entry
Same service taxed differently across the provider's provincial registrations
risks.root_cause: Schedule entries and tariff headings misread, or one province's classification assumed to apply in another province.
risks.title: Wrong service classification or schedule mapping

risks.description: The province whose law applies to a service has not been determined — or two provinces' laws are applied to the same value, or none is. Punjab has verified origin/reverse-charge rules (section 4); for Sindh the provider-office nexus and reverse charge are verified; for KPK, Balochistan and ICT no place-of-provision rules were verified, so the nexus question must be resolved manually. An undetermined jurisdiction is a potential_error, not evidence of intent.
risks.exposure_note: Tax paid to the wrong authority (recoverable/refundable only under that authority's rules) or not paid where due.
risks.followup_action: Map the provider's offices, the recipient's residence and where the service is availed against each candidate province's verified nexus rule (RULE-STP-PUNJAB-JURIS, RULE-STP-SINDH-JURIS); where no rule is verified, obtain advice and record the basis.
risks.potential_financial_effect: Full value of the service taxed at the wrong province's rate, or tax omitted in the correct province.
required_information: Provider's offices/places of business by province
Recipient residence and place of availment
Where the service originates and terminates
Which authority the tax was paid to
risk_indicators: Service provided from one province to a recipient in another with a single provincial tax treatment
Multi-province provider with no apportionment working
No documented nexus analysis for cross-province services
risks.root_cause: Place-of-provision analysis not performed; one province's law assumed for a multi-jurisdiction service.
risks.title: Undetermined provincial jurisdiction for a service

risks.description: The rate charged differs from the verified rate for the province and transaction date — e.g. another province's rate is used (16% in Sindh, 15% in Punjab), a superseded rate is used (13% in Sindh after 1-7-2024), or a notified/schedule rate is missed. Rate-change cut-offs (section 12 equivalents) make the transaction date decisive. A wrong rate is a discrepancy to investigate, not evasion.
risks.exposure_note: Short or excess output tax for the period.
risks.followup_action: Recompute at the verified transaction-date rate (CALC-STP-* tables); correct the return; check the same error across other periods and provinces.
risks.potential_financial_effect: Rate differential × taxable value for each affected transaction.
required_information: Rate applied and its claimed source
Verified transaction-date rate for the province
Transaction dates around rate-change cut-offs
risk_indicators: Rate applied matches a different province's standard rate
Pre-change rate used after a notified rate change
risks.root_cause: Rate tables not updated for the province or the transaction date; cross-province rate confusion.
risks.title: Wrong provincial rate applied for the transaction date

risks.description: A service recorded in the accounts is omitted from the provincial sales tax return — or a taxable service is never recorded at all. Omission may reflect misclassification (service wrongly treated as exempt/out-of-scope), cut-off error, or an unregistered activity. An omission is a potential_error; whether it is a compliance failure depends on the verified taxability analysis.
risks.exposure_note: Undeclared output tax for the period.
risks.followup_action: Reconcile ledger revenue to declared turnover per province (PROC-RECON-SALESTAX); test cut-off; determine taxability of each omitted item under the correct province's rules.
risks.potential_financial_effect: Output tax on the omitted value at the applicable rate.
required_information: Revenue per ledger vs turnover per return, by province
Invoice populations and sequencing
Cut-off testing results
risk_indicators: Ledger revenue exceeds declared turnover with no reconciling items
New service line with no tax treatment analysis
risks.root_cause: Taxability not assessed for a service line; return prepared from incomplete populations; cut-off errors.
risks.title: Service transaction omitted from the return

risks.description: An input tax adjustment, deduction or exemption is claimed without satisfying the statutory conditions — e.g. no valid tax invoice, invoice older than the allowed period, payment not through the banking channel (Punjab s16A / KPK s17), inputs used for reduced-rate services (Punjab s16B(g)-(h), KPK s17), adjustment above 80% of output tax (Punjab s16C), or any adjustment in a province whose provision is unverified (Balochistan, ICT). KPK bars adjustment for below-standard-rate services entirely. An unsupported claim is a discrepancy, not fraud.
risks.exposure_note: Disallowed input tax increases net payable for the period.
risks.followup_action: Run the province's input-tax rule (RULE-STP-*-INPUT) line by line; reverse or qualify claims that fail the conditions; obtain missing invoices or bank proof.
risks.potential_financial_effect: Full amount of the unsupported adjustment/deduction.
required_information: Invoices supporting each input claim and their ages
Payment mode and bank proof
Rate band of the service the inputs relate to
Supplier registration status
risk_indicators: Adjustment claimed on reduced-rate or exempt outputs
risks.root_cause: Statutory conditions for adjustment not tested; another province's (looser) practice assumed.
risks.title: Input tax adjustment or exemption claimed without support

risks.description: Tax collected/charged or payable does not reconcile with the accounting records — e.g. output tax per the sales register differs from the return, tax collected from customers differs from tax deposited, or the tax liability per the computation differs from challans. Unreconciled differences indicate missing, duplicated or mis-period transactions. A difference is an exception_flagged item until each reconciling item is evidenced.
risks.exposure_note: Undeposited collections or unclaimed deposits; misstated liability.
risks.followup_action: Prepare a period-by-period reconciliation (tax charged vs tax declared vs tax deposited); evidence each reconciling item; correct the books or the return.
risks.potential_financial_effect: Unexplained difference between collections, declarations and deposits.
required_information: Output tax per register, return and ledger by period
Challans and bank debits for tax payments
Reconciling items with evidence
risk_indicators: Persistent round-sum differences between register and return
Tax collected from customers but not deposited
Deposits with no corresponding declared liability
risks.root_cause: Return prepared from a different population than the books; deposits misallocated across periods or provinces.
risks.title: Tax collected or payable not reconciling with the accounts

scenarios.accounting_vs_tax: Accounting records the gross consideration for July 2024; tax must be computed at the 15% rate in force when the service was provided (cf. section 12). Services provided in June 2024 remain at the 13% historical rate — the return must not apply one rate to both months.
scenarios.name: Sindh service in July 2024 — 13% to 15% rate cut-over
scenarios.description: A Sindh-registered service provider invoiced services provided in July 2024 but applied the old 13% rate. SRB Notification SRB-3-4/30/2024 moved the standard rate to 15% w.e.f. 1-7-2024, and the substituted section 8(1) (Sindh Finance Act 2025) confirms 15% as the statutory standard rate.

scenarios.accounting_vs_tax: Accounting may carry the input tax as a recoverable; tax law disallows it — the computation must reverse the claim and increase net payable.
scenarios.name: Punjab input tax claimed above the 80% of output tax cap
scenarios.description: A Punjab-registered service provider's monthly return claims input tax adjustment equal to 95% of the period's output tax. Section 16C caps the adjustment at 80% of the output tax for the tax period; the excess must be dealt with per the applicable rules, and each input line must still pass sections 16/16A/16B (valid invoice within six tax periods, banking-channel payment above Rs 50,000, no reduced-rate inputs).

scenarios.accounting_vs_tax: Accounting may carry the input tax as a recoverable; tax law disallows it — the computation must reverse the claim.
scenarios.name: KPK reduced-rate service provider claims input tax adjustment
scenarios.description: A KPK-registered hotel taxed at a reduced Second Schedule rate claims input tax adjustment on its purchases against the reduced-rate output tax. Section 17 bars input tax adjustment for inputs used in services taxed below the 15% standard rate or at specific/fixed rates, and the KPRA Withholding Regulations (Reg. 7) allow adjustment only to standard-rate-or-higher payers for services from registered suppliers.

scenarios.accounting_vs_tax: Accounting books the invoice once; tax analysis must split the jurisdictional treatment — Punjab's rules for the Punjab share, Sindh's reverse-charge analysis for the Sindh recipient — rather than applying one province's rate to the whole value.
scenarios.name: Lahore provider, Karachi recipient — each province's own legislation and rate
scenarios.description: A company with its registered office and service team in Lahore provides consultancy services to a client resident in Karachi. The Punjab office and any non-Punjab presence are separate persons (Punjab s3(3)); Punjab tax is due to the extent the service is charged to Punjab residents or persons availing it in Punjab (Punjab s4(1)/(3)). From the Sindh side, a service provided to a resident person by a non-resident person in the course of an economic activity is a taxable service with the recipient liable under reverse charge (Sindh ss3(2), 9(2)). The engine must therefore select each province's OWN legislation and rate for its share — Punjab's rules and 16% standard rate for the Punjab nexus, Sindh's rules and 15% standard rate for the Sindh reverse-charge analysis — and must not apply one province's rate to the other province's share. If the Sindh recipient is the liable person, the Lahore provider must not also charge Sindh tax on the same value.

scenarios.accounting_vs_tax: Accounting records the invoice value; tax classification decides whether 15% standard or a Schedule-specific rate applies, and whether the entry's conditions (e.g. no input adjustment on reduced rates) hold.
scenarios.name: ICT hotel service — Schedule classification and rate check
scenarios.description: A hotel in Islamabad charges 15% sales tax on room services under the ICT Ordinance. Hotels are a specified Schedule category (section 3(2)), and the FBR-updated Schedule carries service-specific rates for several entries — the provider must verify whether the standard 15% or a Schedule-specific rate applies to the transaction date, and must not assume the treatment from a province's schedule.
